name: Nose bridge filler (nose thread)

card.summary: A minimally invasive procedure that places absorbable threads, sometimes with filler, in the nose to raise the bridge and refine the tip without surgery.
card.aka: PDO nose threads, thread rhinoplasty, non-surgical rhinoplasty
card.note: Reported complications include thread visibility, migration, infection, skin dimpling and granuloma; results are temporary.

quick.overview:
Nose threads are fine absorbable threads, commonly polydioxanone (PDO) and in some reports poly-L-lactic or polycaprolactone, inserted under the skin of the nose to add height and structure to the bridge or tip. People use them to get a straighter, higher or more defined profile without a surgical rhinoplasty, and they are sometimes combined with injectable filler.

Published research is mostly clinician case series and reviews. One series of 553 patients reported high early satisfaction that fell over time, and a 2024 review catalogued the complications seen with the technique.
quick.how: A clinician places the threads through small entry points under local anaesthetic, shaping the nasal contour. Results are visible straight away and are described as temporary, with the threads absorbing over time. People often choose it as a trial of a new nose shape or to avoid surgery.
quick.risks: Reported complications include thread visibility, protrusion into the mouth lining, migration, infection, skin dimpling and granuloma formation. Authors recommend early intervention if problems develop. Treatment by a qualified, regulated clinician is the usual guidance in the literature.

lead: Nose bridge filler with threads, also called nose thread lifting or thread rhinoplasty, is a minimally invasive way of reshaping the nose. Absorbable threads, with or without injectable fillers, are placed to lift the dorsum, support the tip or soften a bump, offering a temporary change in nasal shape without surgery [1][2].

People seek it to improve profile and symmetry, usually as a lower-commitment alternative to surgical rhinoplasty. It is part of the wider non-surgical rhinoplasty field, which uses fillers such as hyaluronic acid and calcium hydroxyapatite to add volume [3].
The published literature consists mainly of a 2023 case series from one surgical group, a 2024 review of complications and a small registered trial.

chain: Absorbable threads placed under the nasal skin
Bridge or tip is raised or supported
Straighter, more defined profile for a limited time
angle.text: Threads add structure to the nose so the bridge looks higher or straighter, with the change visible immediately and described as temporary. They are used as a non-surgical alternative or preview of rhinoplasty.

infobox: PDO, poly-L-lactic and polycaprolactone threads; often combined with fillers

paras: The procedure uses absorbable sutures known as volumizing threads. A 2024 review examined their use in combination with fillers, comparing the precision of nasal contouring with filler-only injections [1]. A 2023 report describes thread lifting of the nose as a relatively recent technique that lacks standardisation, with variable results and short durability, and presents a method using poly-L-lactic and polycaprolactone threads based on graft principles [2].

Filler-based non-surgical rhinoplasty adds volume only and is used cosmetically. Hyaluronic acid filler is temporary and can be dissolved with hyaluronidase, while some other fillers are semi-permanent or permanent [3]. Thread lifts for the face use barbed threads to pull skin upward, and a quoted physician in Wikipedia calls them potentially dangerous in untrained hands [4].

A 2023 series of 553 patients, 471 treated primarily and 82 after previous rhinoplasty, reported a 95 percent satisfaction rate on a global aesthetic improvement questionnaire at 6 months and 62 percent at one year, with mean follow-up of about 33 months [2]. A 2021 registered trial, NCT04769427, enrolled 10 participants to study non-surgical rhinoplasty with PDO threads [5].

A 2024 review of cases described complications including thread visibility, oral mucosa protrusion, migration, skin infection, dimpling and granuloma, along with management and prevention approaches, and stressed early intervention [1].

The adverse effects catalogued in the 2024 review are the main documented harms [1]. Regulation of who may perform thread procedures varies; Wikipedia's thread lift article reports that in the UK aesthetic practitioners need no mandatory qualification [4].

timeline.event: Registered trial NCT04769427 on PDO nose threads begins [5].
Review of adverse effects and prevention published [1].
